flagged.evidence: The cited generic-gallery supplier states that segment directions “are not parallel to any codimension-two direction of the arrangement” (its Statement (1)). This proof excludes only the sets aff({x} ∪ P_j), where P_j are codimension-two intersections in K, before choosing y. Those exclusions do not ensure the segment direction condition. For example, with Φ=A1^3, A=(0,1)^3, x=(1/2,1/2,1/2), and g(A)=(-1,0)×(0,1)^2, take a small simplex S around y0=(-1/2,1/2,1/2). The convex hull K of x and S can have its second and third coordinates in (0.4,0.6), so it contains no codimension-two wall intersections. Then y0 passes the stated exclusions, but [x,y0] is parallel to the codimension-two direction ker B(-,e2) ∩ ker B(-,e3). Thus the proof does not establish that its chosen segment is generic as defined; adding the finitely many sets x+D, one for each codimension-two direction D, closes this short proof gap.
